source_caption:
🎬 Looking for Alaska (2019)

Looking for Alaska follows Miles “Pudge” Halter, a quiet and thoughtful teenager fascinated by famous last words who leaves his ordinary life behind to attend Culver Creek Preparatory School in Alabama. Hoping to discover new experiences and find a deeper meaning in life, Miles quickly becomes friends with his rebellious roommate Chip “The Colonel” Martin and the mysterious, intelligent, and unpredictable Alaska Young. Drawn to Alaska’s captivating personality and complicated outlook on life, Miles finds himself experiencing friendship, romance, and adventure in ways he never imagined. Alongside their close group of friends, they navigate school traditions, elaborate pranks, strict authority figures, and the emotional challenges of growing up. However, beneath Alaska’s confident and carefree appearance lies a troubled young woman struggling with painful memories, guilt, and personal difficulties that few people fully understand. As Miles grows closer to her, his feelings become increasingly complicated, forcing him to confront questions about love, happiness, and the uncertainty of human relationships. When an unexpected tragedy changes their lives, the friends must navigate grief, unanswered questions, and the difficult process of understanding someone they thought they knew. Combining emotional performances, heartfelt storytelling, memorable friendships, and meaningful coming-of-age moments, Looking for Alaska explores love, loss, identity, friendship, guilt, forgiveness, and the search for meaning in life’s most difficult experiences.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Romance • Coming-of-Age

⭐ IMDb: 8.0/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 45–55 minutes per episode • TV-MA

🎥 Creator: Josh Schwartz

✍️ Based on the Novel By: John Green

📺 Where to Watch: Hulu in the United States. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Looking for Alaska is an American teen drama television miniseries created by Josh Schwartz. It is based on the 2005 novel of the same name by John Green. After a film adaptation was repeatedly delayed at Paramount Pictures, Hulu finalized a deal and ordered an eight-episode limited series. It stars Charlie Plummer and Kristine Froseth in the two lead roles as Miles Halter and Alaska Young, respectively. The miniseries premiered on Hulu on October 18, 2019. It received acclaim from critics and fans of the book, with praise geared toward its writing, acting, and faithfulness to the source material.
